system.name: FalconFS
system.one_liner: a distributed file system optimized for large-scale deep learning data pipelines

components.name: Request Queue
components.role: per-request-type ring buffers (create/open/others) that buffer incoming requests

components.name: Worker Thread Pool
components.role: fixed pool of database worker threads that pull batches of requests for processing

components.name: Batch in Transaction
components.role: coalesces requests sharing common near-root path prefixes into one committed batch

components.name: Namespace Replica
components.role: in-memory directory-tree structure locked once per batch instead of once per request

components.name: Inode Table
components.role: inode metadata store locked as part of the batched transaction

components.name: Write-Ahead Log
components.role: durability log the coalesced batch commits to

flows.what: requests coalesced by shared path prefix

content.key_idea: FalconFS's metadata server merges concurrent requests that share common path prefixes into one batched transaction, so three create() calls that would need nine separate locks instead acquire only six by coalescing shared-prefix lock operations.
content.reading_order: top-down: incoming create() calls funnel into the Request Queue, pass through the Worker Thread Pool, and coalesce into a single Batch in Transaction committed against the Database

summary: Figure 8 illustrates FalconFS's concurrent request-merging mechanism inside a metadata server (MNode). Incoming create/open/other requests are funneled into per-type ring-buffer Request Queues (e.g., three create() calls for /a/c, /a/d, and /b/e). A Worker Thread Pool pulls batches of requests from the queues and, because the file namespace is tree-structured, coalesces requests that share common near-root path prefixes into a single Batch in Transaction. Rather than acquiring nine separate locks for the three create operations, the worker locks the shared prefix nodes once, acquiring only six locks total, on the Namespace Replica and Inode Table, before committing the batch to the Write-Ahead Log. The figure demonstrates FalconFS's lock-coalescing optimization for reducing per-request lock overhead under concurrent metadata operations.
summary_zh: 图8展示FalconFS元数据服务器的并发请求合并机制：多个create请求进入环形队列，工作线程池按共享路径前缀将其合并入同一事务批次，仅对命名空间副本和inode表加锁一次，再写入预写日志提交，从而减少锁开销。
